title: LLM inference serving, Part 7: scaling out
tldr: The capstone: serving one model on many GPUs and many requests through a fleet. Why a 70B model needs more than one 80 GB GPU, tensor vs pipeline vs data parallelism (what each splits, what it sends between GPUs, and what it does to TTFT, ITL and throughput), Megatron-style column and row splits with two all-reduces per layer, NVLink vs PCIe and network figures from NVIDIA, the vLLM v0.31.0 flags and logs, disaggregated prefill and decode with KV connectors (experimental in vLLM) and what DistServe, Splitwise and Mooncake argue, the request path from gateway to prefix-aware router to replicas, streaming over SSE and how a disconnect frees KV memory, autoscaling on queue time and KV usage instead of GPU utilization, cold starts, a tested capacity planner that picks a TP size and sizes colocated and disaggregated fleets, failures at 10 times the load, why LLM replicas are stateful and where the sharding and read-replica analogies break, an interview drill, and a final quiz over all seven parts.
